papers.title: TRUSTMEM: Learning Trustworthy Memory Consolidation for LLM Agents with Long-Term Memory
papers.claim: Memory transitions can be evaluated for coverage, preservation, and faithfulness to reduce omission, corruption, and unsupported updates.

hypothesis: A mechanically protected spine preserves required current state and removes superseded state more reliably than ordinary free-form compaction at a comparable token budget.
null_hypothesis: The protected representation does not improve preservation or retains enough stale state to offset its benefit.
independent_variable: Ordinary free-form summary versus protected-spine extraction followed by summary of the remaining context.

variants.name: treatment
variants.description: Mechanical protected-spine extraction plus ordinary remainder summary.

randomness.justification: Model sampling will be frozen with the provider choice.

metrics.acceptance_rule: Treatment requires 100 percent preservation on the frozen mechanical suite; stale retention requires explicit invalidation refinement.

evaluator.rubric: Compare each output to the fixture's required, superseded, conflicting, and untrusted fact labels before judging continuation behavior.
